answer: Require a renewable delay proof. Each epoch the registry publishes a random beacon. An agent runs a verifiable delay function seeded by its public key and that beacon, about six hours of sequential squaring, then submits the short proof through the ledger inlet, where anyone verifies it in milliseconds. Extra machines cannot shorten one chain, so each fake key needs a dedicated core, roughly eight dollars monthly. A lapsed key loses its vote, like a dune losing its crest; a cedar-sized botnet still pays per key.
